html:
Themes and conversation backgrounds

Open Settings → UI Preferences → Edit themes, colors and conversation background, or visit /theme. Desktop and mobile Appearance controls open the same editor. These choices belong to your browser; they do not change the Agent's behavior.

Choose a theme

The library contains 52 day/night pairs: Default, three Low brightness adaptations, 24 established themes, and 24 original world-inspired palettes. Search by name or description, filter by category, or show only Favorites or Modified themes. Established themes include a source link and adaptation note in the preview.

For a screen dimmed while travelling, select the Low brightness filter:

  • Travel Warm uses Gruvbox-inspired parchment by day and warm charcoal at night.
  • Travel Slate uses Nord-inspired cool gray by day and lifted slate at night.
  • Travel Sage uses Everforest-inspired sage by day and forest charcoal at night.

These app adaptations combine tinted day backgrounds and raised night backgrounds with stronger labels and borders. Start with Travel Warm, then preview both variants at your usual screen brightness. They retain the normal Day/Night controls; they do not change your display brightness. Readability still depends on your display and ambient light.

Choose a card to preview it, then select Apply to use it. The header's Day/Night button changes the active variant of the applied pair. Edit day and Edit night choose which variant you are previewing and editing; they do not change the application's saved mode. Existing automatic and system mode preferences continue to work.

A browser Day/Night choice takes precedence over the shared Settings theme mode. Without that override, automatic day/night uses your browser's local time: Day from 06:00 until 18:00, then Night. System mode follows the browser's reported operating-system color scheme. A mode change preserves the separate font-size and high-contrast preferences.

Customize edits colors for text, panels, messages, code, accents, buttons and borders. Enter six-digit hex colors, such as #385a7c, or use the color picker. Invalid visible hex fields disable Apply. The preview reports text contrast below 4.5:1, but does not prevent saving a deliberate low-contrast choice. High contrast and browser forced colors take precedence on application screens.

The font override applies to both variants of that theme. Disable Use existing appearance font to choose a locally available font. Fonts are not downloaded; unavailable families fall back to system fonts. The font picker guide explains detection and browser permission limits. The theme's font override is browser-local, separate from the shared font preference in Settings.

Font weight controls bold styling for both variants of the selected theme. Choose Default for the app's usual emphasis, Regular (no bold) to remove bold styling, or Bold to make all text bold. The preview updates immediately; Apply saves the choice across application screens in this browser. Discard restores the saved choice. Font weight is independent of the selected font family.

Apply, discard and reset

  • Apply saves the selected pair and edits to any themes touched in this editor, along with pending background changes. Other tabs on the same origin update.
  • Discard loads the latest applied preferences, including changes from another tab. Drafts survive switching cards and editor sections within the page, but are not saved across a reload. Leaving with edits requests the browser's warning.
  • A color's Reset, Reset day/night colors, and Reset theme change only drafts until Apply. Reset theme clears that theme's font family and weight overrides as well.
  • Favorites save immediately and are independent of Apply and Discard.
  • Restore Default immediately selects Default and clears its modifiers. It asks before discarding pending edits. Other saved theme modifiers and background settings remain available. Unmodified Default restores each screen's original colors, including the distinct mobile and sign-in defaults.

If another tab changes appearance while you have a draft, the editor retains your draft and reports the change. Apply saves your choices; Discard loads the latest saved ones. These controls do not merge concurrent edits field by field.

Conversation backgrounds

Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP image up to 20 MiB and 40 million pixels. The browser decodes it and prepares a static image with a maximum 2560px edge, requesting WebP encoding. It does not upload the image, send it to the model, or attach it to a conversation.

The image appears inside the conversation viewport across conversations, including mobile and immersive views. It stays outside the header, navigation and composer. User and assistant text appears directly over the image, including in the theme preview. Code blocks and tool/result panels keep their backgrounds. Blur affects only the image. The preview's contrast ratios describe solid palette colors; readability over an image also depends on the image, its visibility and blur. Disabling or removing the image restores normal message backgrounds. High contrast hides conversation wallpaper; forced colors also hide the editor's image preview.

Controls provide visibility from 0–100%, blur from 0–24px, Fill/Fit, horizontal and vertical positioning, enable/disable, replacement and removal. A new empty slot starts with 8px blur, 30% visibility and centered Fill. Replacing an image preserves that slot's existing presentation controls. All these changes remain previews until Apply.

Separate day/night backgrounds initially copies the shared configuration to both variants. Use Edit day/night to change each one. Returning to a shared image retains the separate slots for later use. Removing an image from one slot does not remove it from other slots that still reference it.

Storage and recovery

Palettes, favorites and backgrounds are stored in browser site data. They are not part of the server's Settings export or synchronized to another browser/device. Clearing site data removes them. Background configuration and images stay on the same origin, including its port. The active theme pair and its modifiers can also reach other application service ports on the same hostname through a cookie; other saved pairs, favorites and images do not cross ports this way.

Allow browser storage and free space if saving fails, then retry Apply. A bad image selection leaves the saved image in place. Saving both a theme and background uses separate browser stores: the editor attempts to restore the old background if the theme save fails, but that recovery can also fail when storage is unavailable. After an error, use Discard or reload to inspect the saved state before trying again. If a saved image is missing, select it again; chat remains usable without it.

If a palette does not reach another service port, check that the pages use the same hostname and allow cookies. If colors are difficult to read, Restore Default stays visually distinct from the chosen palette. The implementation guide describes storage ownership, commit ordering and integration boundaries.
